reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in extending the Elo framework beyond binary win/loss to full margin-of-victory distributions. Each handicap threshold becomes a separate binary classifier, with its own Elo rating. This generates a cumulative distribution function (CDF) over all thresholds, which yields the full spread and total distributions. The method assumes that margin distributions are stationary within seasons and that home field is a constant additive shift. The model uses walk-forward validation on 2009–2017 NFL data, comparing predicted CDFs against realized outcomes and Vegas lines. It achieves comparable performance to Vegas but slightly worse, indicating robustness without overfitting. Offseason regression ensures continuity across seasons by retaining 60% of spread ratings and 70% of total ratings, with a fixed 54-Elo point home field advantage. The approach enables GSE to compute P(team beats spread s) for any s and P(total > t) for any t, forming a complete probabilistic game outcome model. The failure mode occurs when thresholds exceed empirical coverage or when regression assumptions break down due to structural change.
